column1: # A BERLIN LEIBHOLZ FAMILY GOT OUT TO SHANGHAI, AND FOUR DOCUMENTS FOLLOW THEM THERE.
# Worked 20 September 2026, from the one clue that started it: a Yad Vashem search on the SUBMITTER
# field returned three relief questionnaires filled in by a SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ "in Shanghai, 1946".
# Who she was, and who she was married to, were unknown four hours ago. They are not now.
# THE BOUND, FIRST. NOTHING BELOW CONNECTS THESE PEOPLE TO KURT'S FAMILY. Albert was born in Berlin,
# not at Schubin. This is a Berlin Leibholz household, and it is the first one this archive has found
# with living people in it — which is why it is written up at all.
field
*** THE CARD THAT ANSWERS IT — CENTRAL LOCATION INDEX, INDEX NO. L 337909 ***
column2: Arolsen Archives DocID 131698324, in 7.14.1 "M.18 — Documentation of the CENTRAL LOCATION INDEX (CLI) of the Joint Distribution Committee in New York", reference 71410001. The CLI was set up by the relief organisations in May 1944 to concentrate data on refugees and the missing, and wound up in 1949.

column1: what the card says, line by line
column2: FAMILY NAME LEIBHOLZ · FIRST NAME ALBERT · M.S. "DIED 8.18.44" · DATE OF BIRTH 5.17.86 · COUNTRY OF BIRTH BERLIN · CITIZENSHIP GERMAN · RELIGION J · OCCUPATION "DEALER" · COUNTRY OF LAST KNOWN ADDRESS SHANGHAI, date 12.14.45.

column1: *** OTHER MEMBERS OF THE FAMILY ABROAD ***
column2: line 2: "SOPHIE · REL. TO NO. 1: W · 6.19.87 · BERLIN". *** W IS WIFE. *** SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ WAS ALBERT'S WIFE, BORN AT BERLIN ON 19 JUNE 1887. The identification that was an inference this morning is a record this afternoon.

column1: and the line that gives the journey
column2: ARR. 6.27.39 FROM BERLIN. They reached Shanghai on 27 JUNE 1939 — six weeks after the census of 17 May, and ten weeks before the war.

column1: *** AND A THIRD PERSON WAS LOOKING FOR THEM ***
column2: APPLICANT: "R.N: CURT STERNGAST, c/o Silman, RAMBAM STR. 39, REHAVIA, JERUSALEM, PALESTINE". Agency reference L-196128 (S-666). Somebody in Jerusalem filed an enquiry about Albert and Sophie, and the CLI answered it with a death and an address.

column1: *** ALBERT'S DEATH, ON THE LIST ITSELF ***
column2: Arolsen DocID 78827389, reference 8808060 — "LISTS CONCERNING JEWISH NATIONALS WHO DIED AND WERE BURIED IN SHANGHAI DURING 1939-1948", 62 documents, acquired from H.I.A.S. in Shanghai via H.I.A.S. in New York. PAGE 24, in the L's: "LEIBHOLZ, ALBERT · 5/17/86 · 8/18/44 · PARALISIS PROGRESSITIS", with the file reference L-142.

column1: so the sequence is complete
column2: BERLIN, an antiques dealer of Halensee in the 1938 directory · ARRIVED SHANGHAI 27 JUNE 1939 · DIED THERE 18 AUGUST 1944, aged 58, of progressive paralysis · his widow SOPHIE still in Shanghai on 14 DECEMBER 1945 and still there in 1946, filling in forms.

column1: what Sophie was doing in 1946
column2: three Relico questionnaires (World Jewish Congress Relief Committee, Geneva; the Shanghai series, the letter L) — for her BROTHER SALLY BINDER, for his wife MATHILDE, and for her BROTHER-IN-LAW HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ. Sister to a Binder and sister-in-law to a Leibholz makes her SOPHIE née BINDER, and the CLI card's "W" makes Albert the Leibholz she married. HEINRICH IS THEREFORE ALBERT'S BROTHER — an inference, and the only step in the chain that is still one.

column1: *** AND IT SEPARATES THE TWO SOPHIES FOR GOOD ***
column2: SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ née BINDER, born BERLIN 19 JUNE 1887, alive in Shanghai in 1946. SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ née ROTHENBERG, born SCHLOCHAU 9 JANUARY 1887, deported Berlin to Auschwitz on 1 March 1943 and murdered. SAME SURNAME, SAME BIRTH YEAR, FIVE MONTHS AND FIVE HUNDRED KILOMETRES APART. Two women, and this archive nearly had one.

column1: HEINRICH, WHO IS THE CONTROL CASE, IS THE SAME MAN IN BOTH FILES
column2: the Relico form gives him as born 16.10.1890, wife AGNES, tax agent, Hornstrasse 19. Mapping the Lives gives "Leibholz, HEINRICH, born 16.10.1890, DIED 9 AUGUST 1948, Leinestr. 32 III. rechts, Neukölln — with AGNES née KERGER, born 10.03.1889". SAME DATE OF BIRTH TO THE DAY, SAME WIFE'S FORENAME. The two records are one man, and Sophie was looking for him from Shanghai two years before he died, not knowing he had survived.

column1: the address that does not match, and what it probably means
column2: HORNSTRASSE 19 against LEINESTRASSE 32. Hornstraße appears nowhere in the Berliner Adressbuch Leibholz entries for 1938 to 1943, and there is no Leibholz at any Hornstraße in the 1939 census. THE LIKELIEST READING IS THAT SOPHIE WROTE DOWN THE ADDRESS SHE LAST KNEW, from before she sailed in June 1939. NOT TESTED — the pre-1938 volumes have not been read.

column1: a clean negative, with its control
column2: LUWINSKI RETURNS NOTHING AT YAD VASHEM — no victim records and no submitter records. Control: the identical query on LEIBHOLZ returns 66 victim records. The Luwinskis were Catholic East Prussians and an absence from a database of Shoah victims is what one would expect; it is now a tested absence rather than an assumption.

column1: source
column2: Yad Vashem, Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names, submitter search, 20 September 2026 · Mapping the Lives, surname LEIBHOLZ with emigration place SHANGHAI, two results · Arolsen Archives DocIDs 131698324 and 78827389, images read the same day with the consent declaration ticked by David.
